## Overview

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 is the MiniCPM-V 4.6 stack with a different `model_type`, so
this adds `MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration` as a subclass of
`MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration` and registers it in the model registry and
the chat-template fallback.

One difference: the image placeholder is counted from the `target_sizes` the
image processor returns instead of being recomputed from the image size, because
the small-image upsize tier is decided from the pixels. This also covers
`adaptive_tile_upsize`, where tiles in one grid no longer share a geometry.

## Additional information

Requires a transformers build that ships `minicpm_ocr` (`MiniCPMOcrConfig`,
`MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor`, `MiniCPMOcrProcessor`).

`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` is needed for plain
transcription, otherwise the template emits `<think>`.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — AI tools were used for part of the code changes.

🔴 If slices in one grid differ in size (the PR claims `adaptive_tile_upsize` does this), the image placeholder token count is wrong and the request fails. The builder reads `tgt_sizes` row 1 only and repeats that count for every slice. The comment says slices share one geometry, which the PR description contradicts. Fix: sum `tgt_sizes[i].prod() // token_divisor` per slice row and emit each `<slice>` with its own count, so every per-tile geometry is covered.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request passes `adaptive_tile_upsize` (or any option that resizes tiles one by one) as a flat `mm_processor_kwargs` key. `_flat_processor_kwargs` (minicpmv4_6.py:164-180) keeps flat keys, so the option reaches the image processor in `process_images`. The PR description says tiles in one grid then no longer share a geometry, so the `target_sizes` rows 1..N differ. `_ocr_image_prompt_text` at minicpm_ocr.py:299-305 takes only `patch_tokens_per_slice[1]` and repeats it `num_rows * num_cols` times. The placeholder token count then no longer matches the vision embeddings built from the real per-slice `tgt_sizes`, so vLLM rejects or aborts the request. The PR claims this case is handled. The `num_rows * num_cols + 1 != tgt_sizes.shape[0]` guard only checks the row count, not that the per-row sizes are equal, so it does not fall back. No test uses unequal slice rows; test_minicpm_ocr.py:307 uses identical `[8, 8]` slices.

**Verification:** In `_ocr_image_prompt_text` (vllm/model_executor/models/minicpm_ocr.py, about lines 299-305), the code uses only one row: `slice_tokens = int(patch_tokens_per_slice[1])` followed by `rows = [slice_ph * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]`. If rows 2..N of `tgt_sizes` differ from row 1, the placeholder token count stops matching the number of embeddings the vision tower produces.

</details>

+        image_idx: int,
+        downsample_mode: str | None,
+        max_slice_nums: int | None,

+
+        ``MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`` counts
+        ``target_sizes.prod(-1) // token_divisor`` per patch, row 0 being the

+        image_end = getattr(tokenizer, "image_end_token", "</image>")
+        slice_start = getattr(tokenizer, "slice_start_token", "<slice>")
+        slice_end = getattr(tokenizer, "slice_end_token", "</slice>")
+        id_start = getattr(tokenizer, "image_id_start_token", "<image_id>")
+        id_end = getattr(tokenizer, "image_id_end_token", "</image_id>")
+
+        placeholder = (
+            f"{id_start}{image_idx}{id_end}"
+            + image_start
+            + image_token * source_tokens
+            + image_end
+        )
+
+        if num_rows > 0 and num_cols > 0:
+            # Slices share one geometry, as `_preprocess` cuts them from a
+            # single refined image.
+            slice_tokens = int(patch_tokens_per_slice[1])
+            if slice_tokens > 0:
+                slice_ph = slice_start + image_token * slice_tokens + slice_end

🔴 Video requests can get a placeholder count that differs from the frame embeddings when the image processor is set to skip or adapt small-image upsizing. This happens with small, unsliced frames. `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` only strips per-request flat keys. The shared image processor still applies its own `disable_small_image_upsize` / `adaptive_small_image_upsize` defaults to each frame. Fix: in `process_videos`, pass explicit values that turn off every upsize option, so frames always upscale the way `_compute_visual_tokens` counts them. Alternatively, count video placeholders from `video_tgt_sizes`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger condition (cannot be checked from this checkout): the `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor` instance has a non-default upsize setting. The checkpoint's preprocessor_config.json could set these defaults. `process_videos` (minicpm_ocr.py:222-230) only removes flat request keys. The 4.6 `process_videos` (minicpmv4_6.py:441) then calls that same instance per frame with no upsize kwargs, so the instance defaults apply. A small frame such as 480x360 (unsliced) stays at native size, or gets an adaptive target. Its `video_tgt_sizes` rows end up smaller than or different from what `get_video_prompt_texts` counts through `_compute_visual_tokens`, whose unsliced branch uses `allow_upscale=True` (minicpm_ocr.py:136-141). The placeholder and embedding counts disagree, which the 4.6 code itself notes makes the engine abort (minicpmv4_6.py:232-234). Images are not affected because they are counted from `tgt_sizes`. Base has no OCR model, so this is new.

**Verification:** Triggering condition: the loaded `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor` instance has a non-default `disable_small_image_upsize` or `adaptive_small_image_upsize` value, and a video has small frames that are not sliced. `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` removes the flat per-request keys and nothing else. The 4.6 `process_videos` (minicpmv4_6.py:402-407) then runs the shared image processor on each frame.

</details>

+            return [0, 0], source_tokens, 0
+
+        best_resize = image_processor.find_best_resize(
+            hf_image_size,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+        )
+        source_tokens = best_resize[0] * best_resize[1] // tokens_per_patch
+
+        refine_size = image_processor.get_refine_size(
+            hf_image_size,
+            grids,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+            allow_upscale=True,
+        )
+        patch_h = refine_size[0] // grids[0]
+        patch_w = refine_size[1] // grids[1]
+        patch_tokens = patch_h * patch_w // tokens_per_patch
+        return grids, source_tokens, patch_tokens
+
+
+class MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor(MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor):
+    def _promote_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Resolve the OCR-only upsize options into the flat form.
+
+        ``process_images`` forwards flat keys only (``_flat_processor_kwargs``
+        drops the nested scopes), and 4.6 recovers just ``downsample_mode`` /
+        ``max_slice_nums`` from the merge. Resolve the OCR options the same way
+        so that a server-level ``mm_processor_kwargs`` value, and the nested
+        ``images_kwargs`` form, both reach the image processor instead of being
+        silently dropped.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+        merged = info._merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(mm_kwargs)
+
+        promoted = {}
+        for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS:
+            value = _scoped_mm_kwarg(merged, "image", key)
+            if value is not None:
+                promoted[key] = value
+
+        if not promoted:
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {**mm_kwargs, **promoted}
+
+    def _drop_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Remove the image-only upsize options from the video path.
+
+        ``process_videos`` runs the *image* processor per frame, so a flat
+        upsize option would reach frames as well. In transformers frames go
+        through ``MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor``, which never applies these, and
+        the video placeholder is counted without them.
+        """
+        if not any(key in mm_kwargs for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS):
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {
+            key: value
+            for key, value in mm_kwargs.items()
+            if key not in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS
+        }
+
+    def process_images(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_images(
+            mm_data,
+            self._promote_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )
+
+    def process_videos(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_videos(
+            mm_data,
+            self._drop_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )

detail.body:
## Overview

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 is the MiniCPM-V 4.6 stack with a different `model_type`, so
this adds `MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration` as a subclass of
`MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration` and registers it in the model registry and
the chat-template fallback.

One difference: the image placeholder is counted from the `target_sizes` the
image processor returns instead of being recomputed from the image size, because
the small-image upsize tier is decided from the pixels. This also covers
`adaptive_tile_upsize`, where tiles in one grid no longer share a geometry.

## Additional information

Requires a transformers build that ships `minicpm_ocr` (`MiniCPMOcrConfig`,
`MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor`, `MiniCPMOcrProcessor`).

`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` is needed for plain
transcription, otherwise the template emits `<think>`.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — AI tools were used for part of the code changes.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniCPM-OCR semantics that differ from MiniCPM-V 4.6.
+
+The model code is inherited wholesale, so what needs pinning is the image
+geometry: the `"4x"` patch-grid alignment, and the fact that the image
+placeholder is measured from the `target_sizes` the image processor returned
+rather than recomputed from the image dimensions.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.models.minicpm_ocr import (
+    _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS,
+    MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor,
+    MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models.minicpmv4_6 import MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor
+from vllm.multimodal.parse import ImageSize
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+
+_PATCH_SIZE = 14
+_SCALE_RESOLUTION = 448
+
+
+def ensure_divide(length: int, divisor: int) -> int:
+    """Copy of `transformers.models.minicpmv4_6...ensure_divide`."""
+    return max(round(length / divisor) * divisor, divisor)
+
+
+class _StubImageProcessor:
+    """Stands in for `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor`.
+
+    `find_best_resize` and `get_sliced_grid`/`get_refine_size` are transcribed
+    from `modular_minicpm_ocr.py` / `image_processing_minicpmv4_6.py` so the
+    geometry under test is the real one, without needing a checkpoint or an
+    installed transformers build that carries the model.
+    """
+
+    downsample_mode = "4x"
+    max_slice_nums = 9
+    scale_resolution = _SCALE_RESOLUTION
+    patch_size = _PATCH_SIZE
+    slice_mode = True
+
+    def find_best_resize(
+        self, image_size, scale_resolution, patch_size, allow_upscale=False
+    ):
+        height, width = image_size
+        if (height * width > scale_resolution * scale_resolution) or allow_upscale:
+            aspect_ratio = width / height
+            height = int(scale_resolution / math.sqrt(aspect_ratio))
+            width = int(height * aspect_ratio)
+        # The OCR delta: one 2x2 merge in "4x" mode, two in "16x".
+        merge_factor = 2 if self.downsample_mode == "4x" else 4
+        best_width = ensure_divide(width, patch_size * merge_factor)
+        best_height = ensure_divide(height, patch_size * merge_factor)
+        return best_height, best_width
+
+    def get_refine_size(
+        self, image_size, grid, scale_resolution, patch_size, allow_upscale=False
+    ):
+        height, width = image_size
+        grid_y, grid_x = grid
+        refine_width = ensure_divide(width, grid_x)
+        refine_height = ensure_divide(height, grid_y)
+        best_height, best_width = self.find_best_resize(
+            (refine_height / grid_y, refine_width / grid_x),
+            scale_resolution,
+            patch_size,
+            allow_upscale=allow_upscale,
+        )
+        return best_height * grid_y, best_width * grid_x
+
+    def get_sliced_grid(self, image_size, max_slice_nums, scale_resolution):
+        original_height, original_width = image_size
+        log_ratio = math.log(original_width / original_height)
+        ratio = original_width * original_height / (scale_resolution**2)
+        multiple = min(math.ceil(ratio), max_slice_nums)
+        if multiple <= 1:
+            return None
+
+        candidate_split_grids_nums = []
+        for i in [multiple - 1, multiple, multiple + 1]:
+            if i == 1 or i > max_slice_nums:
+                continue
+            candidate_split_grids_nums.append(i)
+
+        candidate_grids = []
+        for split_grids_nums in candidate_split_grids_nums:
+            m = 1
+            while m <= split_grids_nums:
+                if split_grids_nums % m == 0:
+                    candidate_grids.append([m, split_grids_nums // m])
+                m += 1
+
+        best_grid = [1, 1]
+        min_error = float("inf")
+        for grid in candidate_grids:
+            error = abs(log_ratio - math.log(grid[0] / grid[1]))
+            if error < min_error:
+                best_grid = grid
+                min_error = error
+        return best_grid
+
+
+class _StubTokenizer:
+    image_token = "<|image_pad|>"
+    image_start_token = "<image>"
+    image_end_token = "</image>"
+    slice_start_token = "<slice>"
+    slice_end_token = "</slice>"
+    image_id_start_token = "<image_id>"
+    image_id_end_token = "</image_id>"
+
+
+def _make_info(**processor_attrs) -> MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo:
+    info = MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo.__new__(MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+    image_processor = _StubImageProcessor()
+    for key, value in processor_attrs.items():
+        setattr(image_processor, key, value)
+
+    info.get_image_processor = lambda **kwargs: image_processor  # type: ignore[method-assign]
+    info.get_tokenizer = lambda: _StubTokenizer()  # type: ignore[method-assign,return-value]
+    return info
+
+
+def _make_processor(info: MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo):
+    processor = MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor.__new__(MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor)
+    processor.info = info
+    return processor
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Geometry: "4x" aligns to patch_size * 2, not patch_size * 4
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_4x_mode_aligns_the_patch_grid_to_two_patches():
+    """The resize grid follows the number of 2x2 merges, not just the divisor.
+
+    `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize` aligns to `patch_size * 2` in
+    `"4x"` mode, so a 4.6-style alignment would round the grid to a different
+    size and the vision tower and the placeholder would disagree.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=300, height=200)
+
+    grids_4x, source_4x, patch_4x = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+    grids_16x, source_16x, patch_16x = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="16x"
+    )
+
+    # Not sliced: 300*200 < 448^2.
+    assert grids_4x == [0, 0]
+    assert grids_16x == [0, 0]
+    assert patch_4x == 0 and patch_16x == 0
+
+    # Upscaled to ~448 on the long side, then aligned: "4x" rounds to 28px and
+    # "16x" to 56px, which lands on a different grid for the same image.
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("4x").find_best_resize(
+        (200, 300), _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    ) == (364, 560)
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("16x").find_best_resize(
+        (200, 300), _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    ) == (392, 560)
+
+    # 364*560 / (14*14*4) = 260 against 392*560 / (14*14*16) = 70: the ratio is
+    # not a clean 4x precisely because the alignment differs, which is what a
+    # 4.6-style `find_best_resize` would get wrong.
+    assert source_4x == 260
+    assert source_16x == 70
+
+
+def test_pinned_processor_does_not_mutate_the_shared_instance():
+    """A per-request mode must not leak into the shared image processor.
+
+    `find_best_resize` reads `downsample_mode` off the instance, and the engine
+    reuses one processor across requests.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    shared = info.get_image_processor()
+    assert shared.downsample_mode == "4x"
+
+    pinned = info._pinned_image_processor("16x")
+    assert pinned is not shared
+    assert pinned.downsample_mode == "16x"
+    assert shared.downsample_mode == "4x"
+
+    # The default mode needs no copy at all.
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("4x") is shared
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor(None) is shared
+
+
+def test_downsample_mode_defaults_to_the_processor_value():
+    """OCR checkpoints ship `downsample_mode: "4x"`; 4.6's fallback is "16x"."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    assert info._get_downsample_mode() == "4x"
+    assert info._get_downsample_mode("16x") == "16x"
+
+    # The fallback only applies when the processor carries no value at all.
+    bare = _make_info()
+    del type(bare.get_image_processor()).downsample_mode
+    try:
+        assert bare._get_downsample_mode() == "16x"
+    finally:
+        _StubImageProcessor.downsample_mode = "4x"
+
+
+def test_sliced_image_token_counts_match_the_transformers_divisor():
+    """Sliced geometry: source + grid*patch tokens, counted with divisor 4."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+
+    grids, source_tokens, patch_tokens = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+
+    assert grids != [0, 0]
+    processor = info._pinned_image_processor("4x")
+    refine = processor.get_refine_size(
+        (1120, 1680), grids, _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    )
+    expected_patch = (
+        (refine[0] // grids[0])
+        * (refine[1] // grids[1])
+        // (_PATCH_SIZE * _PATCH_SIZE * 4)
+    )
+    assert patch_tokens == expected_patch
+    assert source_tokens > 0
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Placeholder measured from target_sizes
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _placeholder(info, tgt_sizes, image_size, *, image_idx=0, mode="4x"):
+    processor = _make_processor(info)
+    return processor._ocr_image_prompt_text(
+        torch.tensor(tgt_sizes, dtype=torch.long),
+        image_size,
+        image_idx,
+        downsample_mode=mode,
+        max_slice_nums=None,
+    )
+
+
+def test_placeholder_is_counted_from_target_sizes():
+    """Token count mirrors `MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`.
+
+    That method computes `target_sizes.prod(-1) // token_divisor` per patch.
+    Reproducing it here is what keeps the count right under
+    `adaptive_small_image_upsize`, whose resize target is decided from the
+    pixels and so is invisible to a size-only computation.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    # An unsliced image: one row only.
+    text = _placeholder(info, [[8, 8]], ImageSize(width=112, height=112))
+
+    # 8*8 = 64 patches, divisor 4 -> 16 tokens.
+    assert text == ("<image_id>0</image_id><image>" + "<|image_pad|>" * 16 + "</image>")
+
+
+def test_adaptive_upsize_changes_the_count_without_changing_the_image_size():
+    """Two tiers of the same image must yield different placeholders.
+
+    `adaptive_upsize_tier` can send a small image to `scale_resolution` or to
+    `adaptive_upsize_tiny_target_resolution`, and `ImageSize` is identical in
+    both cases. This is exactly the divergence that counting from `image_size`
+    would miss.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=80, height=80)
+
+    native = _placeholder(info, [[4, 4]], image_size)
+    tier2 = _placeholder(info, [[6, 6]], image_size)
+    tier1 = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]], image_size)
+
+    assert native.count("<|image_pad|>") == 4
+    assert tier2.count("<|image_pad|>") == 9
+    assert tier1.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64
+
+    # And the size-only path cannot tell them apart: it always upscales to
+    # `scale_resolution`, so all three tiers would be counted as 448*448 worth
+    # of tokens regardless of what the processor actually produced.
+    _, size_only_tokens, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+    assert size_only_tokens == 256
+    assert size_only_tokens not in (4, 9, 64)
+
+
+def test_placeholder_emits_the_slice_grid_from_the_geometry():
+    """Slice rows come from `get_sliced_grid`, which is not pixel-dependent."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+    grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(image_size, downsample_mode="4x")
+    num_slices = grids[0] * grids[1]
+
+    tgt_sizes = [[16, 16]] + [[8, 8]] * num_slices
+    text = _placeholder(info, tgt_sizes, image_size)
+
+    assert text is not None
+    assert text.count("<slice>") == num_slices
+    assert text.count("\n") == grids[0] - 1
+    # 16*16/4 source tokens + one 8*8/4 block per slice.
+    assert text.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64 + 16 * num_slices
+
+
+def test_placeholder_emits_differing_tiles_one_by_one():
+    """`adaptive_tile_upsize` can leave tiles at different resolutions.
+
+    Each slice then gets its own count instead of row 1 repeated.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+    grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(image_size, downsample_mode="4x")
+    num_rows, num_cols = grids
+    num_slices = num_rows * num_cols
+
+    tile_sizes = [[8 + (i % 2) * 4, 8 + (i % 2) * 4] for i in range(num_slices)]
+    text = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]] + tile_sizes, image_size)
+
+    assert text is not None
+    assert text.count("<slice>") == num_slices
+    per_tile = sum(size[0] * size[1] // 4 for size in tile_sizes)
+    assert text.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64 + per_tile
+
+
+def test_video_path_pins_the_upsize_defaults(monkeypatch):
+    """Frames must be counted the same way `_compute_visual_tokens` counts them.
+
+    `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` only removes request keys; the loaded processor
+    still applies its own defaults per frame, so they are pinned too.
+    """
+    captured = {}
+
+    def fake_process_videos(self, mm_data, mm_kwargs):
+        captured.update(mm_kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor, "process_videos", fake_process_videos
+    )
+    processor = _processor_with_merge({})
+    processor.process_videos(
+        {},
+        {"downsample_mode": "4x", "adaptive_small_image_upsize": True},
+    )
+
+    assert captured["downsample_mode"] == "4x"
+    assert captured["adaptive_small_image_upsize"] is False
+    assert captured["disable_small_image_upsize"] is False
+    assert captured["adaptive_tile_upsize"] is False
+
+
+def test_placeholder_falls_back_when_target_sizes_disagree_with_the_grid():
+    """A mismatch must not silently emit a count we cannot justify.
+
+    Returning `None` leaves the caller on the inherited 4.6 path instead of
+    producing a placeholder whose length the vision tower will not match.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+
+    # Only the thumbnail row, while the geometry says the image is sliced.
+    assert _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]], image_size) is None
+    # Malformed tables.
+    assert _placeholder(info, [[16, 16, 16]], ImageSize(width=112, height=112)) is None
+    # A zero-token source.
+    assert _placeholder(info, [[1, 1]], ImageSize(width=112, height=112)) is None
+
+
+def test_placeholder_uses_the_divisor_of_the_resolved_mode():
+    """`token_divisor` follows the same resolved mode as the pixel path."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=112, height=112)
+
+    text_4x = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]], image_size, mode="4x")
+    text_16x = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]], image_size, mode="16x")
+
+    assert text_4x.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64
+    assert text_16x.count("<|image_pad|>") == 16
+
+
+def test_placeholder_carries_the_local_image_id():
+    info = _make_info()
+    text = _placeholder(info, [[8, 8]], ImageSize(width=112, height=112), image_idx=3)
+    assert text.startswith("<image_id>3</image_id><image>")
+
+
+def _transformers_replace_image_token(
+    target_sizes, grids, num_patches_per_image, image_idx, image_token_divisor
+):
+    """Transcription of `MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`.
+
+    Kept verbatim (minus the tokenizer attribute lookups) so the count under
+    test is compared against the transformers formula itself rather than
+    against a number restated in the assertion. Note the divisor is applied to
+    `target_sizes` directly: that tensor is already in patch units.
+    """
+    cum_patches = np.cumsum(num_patches_per_image)
+    start_idx = cum_patches[image_idx - 1] if image_idx > 0 else 0
+    end_idx = cum_patches[image_idx]
+    img_target_sizes = target_sizes[start_idx:end_idx]
+    num_tokens_per_patch = img_target_sizes.prod(-1) // image_token_divisor
+    num_rows, num_cols = grids[image_idx]
+
+    image_placeholder = (
+        "<image>" + "<|image_pad|>" * int(num_tokens_per_patch[0]) + "</image>"
+    )
+    if num_rows > 0 and num_cols > 0:
+        per_slice = int(num_tokens_per_patch[1]) if len(num_tokens_per_patch) > 1 else 0
+        slice_placeholder = "<slice>" + "<|image_pad|>" * per_slice + "</slice>"
+        slices = [slice_placeholder * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]
+        image_placeholder += "\n".join(slices)
+    return image_placeholder
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "width,height,mode",
+    [
+        (112, 112, "4x"),
+        (112, 112, "16x"),
+        (300, 200, "4x"),
+        (1680, 1120, "4x"),
+        (1680, 1120, "16x"),
+        (2048, 512, "4x"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_placeholder_matches_the_transformers_formula(width, height, mode):
+    """End-to-end agreement with `replace_image_token` on real geometry.
+
+    `target_sizes` is derived the way `_preprocess` does (`size // patch_size`
+    per patch), then both implementations are asked for the placeholder. This
+    is the check that pins the divisor: `target_sizes` is in patch units, so
+    dividing by `patch_size ** 2 * token_divisor` here -- as the pixel-side
+    `_compute_visual_tokens` correctly does -- would undercount by 196x.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=width, height=height)
+    processor = info._pinned_image_processor(mode)
+    grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(image_size, downsample_mode=mode)
+
+    # Rebuild `target_sizes` exactly as `_preprocess` records it.
+    sliced = grids != [0, 0]
+    source_h, source_w = processor.find_best_resize(
+        (height, width), _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=not sliced
+    )
+    target_sizes = [[source_h // _PATCH_SIZE, source_w // _PATCH_SIZE]]
+    if sliced:
+        refine_h, refine_w = processor.get_refine_size(
+            (height, width), grids, _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+        )
+        patch_h, patch_w = refine_h // grids[0], refine_w // grids[1]
+        target_sizes += [[patch_h // _PATCH_SIZE, patch_w // _PATCH_SIZE]] * (
+            grids[0] * grids[1]
+        )
+

+    """The two divisors must land on the same count for the plain path.

+    while `_ocr_image_prompt_text` divides patch counts by `divisor` alone.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Inference-only MiniCPM-OCR model.
+
+Same vision/LLM stack as MiniCPM-V 4.6. ``MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration``
+is a plain subclass of ``MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration`` in transformers
+too; what differs is the image geometry:
+
+* ``downsample_mode`` defaults to ``"4x"``, and in that mode
+  ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize`` aligns the patch grid to
+  ``patch_size * 2`` instead of ``patch_size * 4``, because ``"4x"`` goes
+  through one 2x2 merge (downsample MLP) rather than two (ViT insert merger as
+  well).
+* An image small enough not to be sliced may be resized to a target picked from
+  its own pixels (``adaptive_small_image_upsize``) or kept at its native
+  resolution (``disable_small_image_upsize``).
+
+The second point is why the image placeholder here is measured from the
+``target_sizes`` the image processor actually returned rather than recomputed
+from the image dimensions: the adaptive tier is decided by an Otsu threshold
+plus connected-component analysis over the pixels, which a size-only
+reimplementation cannot reproduce. This mirrors
+``MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token``, which reads the same tensor.
+"""
+
+import copy
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import replace as dataclass_replace
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+from vllm.multimodal.parse import ImageProcessorItems, ImageSize
+from vllm.multimodal.processing.processor import (
+    PromptUpdateDetails,
+    cached_encode,
+)
+
+from .minicpmv import MiniCPMVDummyInputsBuilder, MiniCPMVImageEmbeddingItems
+from .minicpmv4_6 import (
+    MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration,
+    MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor,
+    MiniCPMV4_6ProcessingInfo,
+    _scoped_mm_kwarg,
+)
+
+# Options declared by `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessorKwargs` on top of the 4.6 set.
+# `MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessorKwargs` deliberately declares none of them: in
+# transformers videos go through `MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor`, which has no
+# small-image upsize logic at all.
+_OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS = (
+    "disable_small_image_upsize",
+    "adaptive_small_image_upsize",
+    "adaptive_upsize_font_px",
+    "adaptive_upsize_dense_per_kpx",
+    "adaptive_upsize_tiny_pixels",
+    "adaptive_upsize_tiny_target_resolution",
+    "adaptive_tile_upsize",
+)
+
+# Pinned for video frames: `_compute_visual_tokens` counts an unsliced frame as
+# upscaled to `scale_resolution` with uniform tiles, but `process_videos` runs
+# the image processor, whose own defaults are not visible to that count.
+_VIDEO_PINNED_UPSIZE_KWARGS = {
+    "disable_small_image_upsize": False,
+    "adaptive_small_image_upsize": False,
+    "adaptive_tile_upsize": False,
+}
+
+
+class MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo(MiniCPMV4_6ProcessingInfo):
+    def _pinned_image_processor(self, downsample_mode: str | None = None):
+        """Image processor view pinned to the mode resolved for this request.
+
+        ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize`` reads ``downsample_mode``
+        off the instance, so a per-request override only reaches it through the
+        shallow copy that ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.__call__`` makes. Measure
+        the token count on a copy pinned the same way, otherwise the pixels are
+        aligned to one grid and the placeholder is counted on another.
+        """
+        image_processor = self.get_image_processor()
+        resolved = self._get_downsample_mode(downsample_mode)
+        if getattr(image_processor, "downsample_mode", None) == resolved:
+            return image_processor
+
+        pinned = copy.copy(image_processor)
+        pinned.downsample_mode = resolved
+        return pinned
+
+    def get_image_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize:
+        # OCR-only override: source the dummy-input dimension from the image
+        # processor's `scale_resolution` (the slice resize target) rather than the
+        # top-level `config.image_size`. The top-level field is dropped from
+        # `MiniCPMOcrConfig`, and the existing default of 448 was always equal to
+        # `scale_resolution` here. `vision_config.image_size` is the ViT patch grid
+        # (980 for this checkpoint), not the preprocessed image dimension, so it is
+        # not the right value for dummy-input sizing.
+        image_size = self.get_image_processor().scale_resolution
+        max_slice_num = self.get_image_max_slice_num()
+        return ImageSize(width=image_size, height=image_size * max_slice_num)
+
+    def get_video_frame_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize:
+        # See `get_image_size_with_most_features` for why OCR sources from
+        # `scale_resolution` instead of the (now-removed) top-level `config.image_size`.
+        image_size = self.get_image_processor().scale_resolution
+        max_slice_num = self.get_video_max_slice_num()
+        return ImageSize(width=image_size, height=image_size * max_slice_num)
+
+    def _compute_visual_tokens(
+        self,
+        image_size: ImageSize,
+        max_slice_nums: int | None = None,
+        downsample_mode: str | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[list[int], int, int]:
+        """Grid, source tokens and per-slice tokens for one image.
+
+        Same contract as 4.6, re-derived on the pinned processor so that the
+        ``"4x"`` patch-grid alignment is applied.
+
+        The unsliced branch upscales to ``scale_resolution``, which is what
+        ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor._preprocess`` does for the default options
+        and what the video path does unconditionally. The remaining
+        ``*_small_image_upsize`` combinations depend on the pixels, so for
+        images the placeholder is taken from ``target_sizes`` instead; see
+        ``MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor._ocr_image_prompt_text``.
+        """
+        image_processor = self._pinned_image_processor(downsample_mode)
+        if max_slice_nums is None:
+            max_slice_nums = image_processor.max_slice_nums
+
+        patch_size = image_processor.patch_size
+        scale_res = image_processor.scale_resolution
+        token_divisor = 4 if image_processor.downsample_mode == "4x" else 16
+        tokens_per_patch = patch_size * patch_size * token_divisor
+
+        # vLLM ImageSize is (width, height); transformers expects (height, width)
+        hf_image_size = (image_size.height, image_size.width)
+
+        grids = image_processor.get_sliced_grid(
+            hf_image_size,
+            max_slice_nums,
+            scale_res,
+        )
+
+        if grids is None:
+            best_size = image_processor.find_best_resize(
+                hf_image_size,
+                scale_res,
+                patch_size,
+                allow_upscale=True,
+            )
+            source_tokens = best_size[0] * best_size[1] // tokens_per_patch
+            return [0, 0], source_tokens, 0
+
+        best_resize = image_processor.find_best_resize(
+            hf_image_size,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+        )
+        source_tokens = best_resize[0] * best_resize[1] // tokens_per_patch
+
+        refine_size = image_processor.get_refine_size(
+            hf_image_size,
+            grids,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+            allow_upscale=True,
+        )
+        patch_h = refine_size[0] // grids[0]
+        patch_w = refine_size[1] // grids[1]
+        patch_tokens = patch_h * patch_w // tokens_per_patch
+        return grids, source_tokens, patch_tokens
+
+
+class MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor(MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor):
+    def _promote_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Resolve the OCR-only upsize options into the flat form.
+
+        ``process_images`` forwards flat keys only (``_flat_processor_kwargs``
+        drops the nested scopes), and 4.6 recovers just ``downsample_mode`` /
+        ``max_slice_nums`` from the merge. Resolve the OCR options the same way
+        so that a server-level ``mm_processor_kwargs`` value, and the nested
+        ``images_kwargs`` form, both reach the image processor instead of being
+        silently dropped.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+        merged = info._merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(mm_kwargs)
+
+        promoted = {}
+        for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS:
+            value = _scoped_mm_kwarg(merged, "image", key)
+            if value is not None:
+                promoted[key] = value
+
+        if not promoted:
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {**mm_kwargs, **promoted}
+
+    def _drop_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Remove the image-only upsize options from the video path.
+
+        ``process_videos`` runs the *image* processor per frame, so a flat
+        upsize option would reach frames as well. In transformers frames go
+        through ``MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor``, which never applies these, and
+        the video placeholder is counted without them.
+        """
+        if not any(key in mm_kwargs for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS):
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {
+            key: value
+            for key, value in mm_kwargs.items()
+            if key not in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS
+        }
+
+    def process_images(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_images(
+            mm_data,
+            self._promote_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )
+
+    def process_videos(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_videos(
+            mm_data,
+            {
+                **self._drop_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+                **_VIDEO_PINNED_UPSIZE_KWARGS,
+            },
+        )
+
+    def _ocr_image_prompt_text(
+        self,
+        tgt_sizes: torch.Tensor,
+        image_size: ImageSize,
+        image_idx: int,
+        downsample_mode: str | None,
+        max_slice_nums: int | None,
+    ) -> str | None:
+        """Placeholder text for one image, measured from its ``target_sizes``.
+
+        ``MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`` counts
+        ``target_sizes.prod(-1) // token_divisor`` per patch, row 0 being the
+        source image and row 1 a slice. Doing the same here keeps the count
+        correct for ``adaptive_small_image_upsize``, whose resize target is
+        decided from the pixels and cannot be recovered from ``image_size``.
+
+        ``target_sizes`` is already in *patch* units -- the image processor
+        stores ``source_h // patch_size`` -- so the divisor here is the bare
+        ``token_divisor``, unlike the pixel-side computation in
+        ``_compute_visual_tokens`` which also divides by ``patch_size ** 2``.
+
+        The slice grid is not pixel-dependent (``get_sliced_grid`` is a
+        function of the image size, ``max_slice_nums`` and
+        ``scale_resolution``), so it still comes from the geometry helper.
+        Returns ``None`` when the two disagree, leaving the caller on the 4.6
+        path rather than emitting a count we cannot justify.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+
+        if tgt_sizes.ndim != 2 or tgt_sizes.shape[-1] != 2 or tgt_sizes.shape[0] < 1:
+            return None
+
+        image_processor = info._pinned_image_processor(downsample_mode)
+        token_divisor = 4 if image_processor.downsample_mode == "4x" else 16
+
+        grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+            image_size,
+            max_slice_nums,
+            downsample_mode=downsample_mode,
+        )
+        num_rows, num_cols = grids[0], grids[1]
+        if num_rows * num_cols + 1 != tgt_sizes.shape[0]:
+            return None
+
+        patch_tokens_per_slice = (
+            tgt_sizes.to(torch.long).prod(-1) // token_divisor
+        ).tolist()
+        source_tokens = int(patch_tokens_per_slice[0])
+        if source_tokens <= 0:
+            return None
+
+        tokenizer = info.get_tokenizer()
+        image_token = getattr(tokenizer, "image_token", "<|image_pad|>")
+        image_start = getattr(tokenizer, "image_start_token", "<image>")
+        image_end = getattr(tokenizer, "image_end_token", "</image>")
+        slice_start = getattr(tokenizer, "slice_start_token", "<slice>")
+        slice_end = getattr(tokenizer, "slice_end_token", "</slice>")
+        id_start = getattr(tokenizer, "image_id_start_token", "<image_id>")
+        id_end = getattr(tokenizer, "image_id_end_token", "</image_id>")
+
+        placeholder = (
+            f"{id_start}{image_idx}{id_end}"
+            + image_start
+            + image_token * source_tokens
+            + image_end
+        )
+
+        if num_rows > 0 and num_cols > 0:
+            # `adaptive_tile_upsize` classifies each tile on its own crop, so
+            # slices in one grid can differ; emit one placeholder per tile.
+            tile_tokens = [int(t) for t in patch_tokens_per_slice[1:]]
+            if len(set(tile_tokens)) <= 1:
+                slice_tokens = tile_tokens[0] if tile_tokens else 0
+                if slice_tokens > 0:
+                    slice_ph = slice_start + image_token * slice_tokens + slice_end
+                    rows = [slice_ph * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]
+                    placeholder += "\n".join(rows)
+            else:
+                if len(tile_tokens) != num_rows * num_cols:
+                    return None
+                rows = []
+                for r in range(num_rows):
+                    line = []
+                    for c in range(num_cols):
+                        n = tile_tokens[r * num_cols + c]
+                        if n > 0:
+                            line.append(slice_start + image_token * n + slice_end)
+                    rows.append("".join(line))
+                placeholder += "\n".join(rows)
+
+        return placeholder
+
+    def _get_prompt_updates(
+        self,
+        mm_items,
+        hf_processor_mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+        out_mm_kwargs,
+    ):
+        updates = super()._get_prompt_updates(
+            mm_items,
+            hf_processor_mm_kwargs,
+            out_mm_kwargs,
+        )
+
+        image_ds_mode = self._resolve_downsample_mode(
+            hf_processor_mm_kwargs, modality="image"
+        )
+        image_max_slice = self._resolve_max_slice_nums(hf_processor_mm_kwargs)
+
+        tokenizer = self.info.get_tokenizer()
+        image_embed_text = getattr(tokenizer, "image_token", "<|image_pad|>")
+        image_embed_ids = [tokenizer.get_vocab()[image_embed_text]]
+        image_items = out_mm_kwargs.get("image")
+
+        def ocr_image_replacement(item_idx: int, fallback):
+            tgt_sizes = None
+            if image_items is not None and item_idx < len(image_items):
+                tgt_elem = image_items[item_idx].get("tgt_sizes")
+                if tgt_elem is not None and isinstance(tgt_elem.data, torch.Tensor):
+                    tgt_sizes = tgt_elem.data
+
+            if tgt_sizes is None:
+                # Image embeddings bypass the image processor, so there is no
+                # `target_sizes` to measure and no pixel-dependent resize.
+                return fallback(item_idx)
+
+            images = mm_items.get_items(
+                "image",
+                (MiniCPMVImageEmbeddingItems, ImageProcessorItems),
+            )
+            text = self._ocr_image_prompt_text(
+                tgt_sizes,
+                images.get_image_size(item_idx),
+                item_idx,
+                downsample_mode=image_ds_mode,
+                max_slice_nums=image_max_slice,
+            )
+            if text is None:
+                return fallback(item_idx)
+
+            return PromptUpdateDetails.select_token_ids(
+                cached_encode(tokenizer, text, add_special_tokens=False),
+                image_embed_ids,
+            )
+
+        def with_ocr_replacement(update):
+            fallback = update.replacement
+            return dataclass_replace(
+                update,
+                replacement=lambda item_idx: ocr_image_replacement(item_idx, fallback),
+            )
+
+        return [
+            with_ocr_replacement(update) if update.modality == "image" else update
+            for update in updates
+        ]
+
+
+@MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.register_processor(
+    MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor,
+    info=MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo,
+    dummy_inputs=MiniCPMVDummyInputsBuilder,
+)
+class MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration(MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration):
+    def _drop_vision_last_layer(self) -> bool:

🔴 If slices in one grid differ in size (the PR claims `adaptive_tile_upsize` does this), the image placeholder token count is wrong and the request fails. The builder reads `tgt_sizes` row 1 only and repeats that count for every slice. The comment says slices share one geometry, which the PR description contradicts. Fix: sum `tgt_sizes[i].prod() // token_divisor` per slice row and emit each `<slice>` with its own count, so every per-tile geometry is covered.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request passes `adaptive_tile_upsize` (or any option that resizes tiles one by one) as a flat `mm_processor_kwargs` key. `_flat_processor_kwargs` (minicpmv4_6.py:164-180) keeps flat keys, so the option reaches the image processor in `process_images`. The PR description says tiles in one grid then no longer share a geometry, so the `target_sizes` rows 1..N differ. `_ocr_image_prompt_text` at minicpm_ocr.py:299-305 takes only `patch_tokens_per_slice[1]` and repeats it `num_rows * num_cols` times. The placeholder token count then no longer matches the vision embeddings built from the real per-slice `tgt_sizes`, so vLLM rejects or aborts the request. The PR claims this case is handled. The `num_rows * num_cols + 1 != tgt_sizes.shape[0]` guard only checks the row count, not that the per-row sizes are equal, so it does not fall back. No test uses unequal slice rows; test_minicpm_ocr.py:307 uses identical `[8, 8]` slices.

**Verification:** In `_ocr_image_prompt_text` (vllm/model_executor/models/minicpm_ocr.py, about lines 299-305), the code uses only one row: `slice_tokens = int(patch_tokens_per_slice[1])` followed by `rows = [slice_ph * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]`. If rows 2..N of `tgt_sizes` differ from row 1, the placeholder token count stops matching the number of embeddings the vision tower produces.

</details>

🔴 Video requests can get a placeholder count that differs from the frame embeddings when the image processor is set to skip or adapt small-image upsizing. This happens with small, unsliced frames. `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` only strips per-request flat keys. The shared image processor still applies its own `disable_small_image_upsize` / `adaptive_small_image_upsize` defaults to each frame. Fix: in `process_videos`, pass explicit values that turn off every upsize option, so frames always upscale the way `_compute_visual_tokens` counts them. Alternatively, count video placeholders from `video_tgt_sizes`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger condition (cannot be checked from this checkout): the `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor` instance has a non-default upsize setting. The checkpoint's preprocessor_config.json could set these defaults. `process_videos` (minicpm_ocr.py:222-230) only removes flat request keys. The 4.6 `process_videos` (minicpmv4_6.py:441) then calls that same instance per frame with no upsize kwargs, so the instance defaults apply. A small frame such as 480x360 (unsliced) stays at native size, or gets an adaptive target. Its `video_tgt_sizes` rows end up smaller than or different from what `get_video_prompt_texts` counts through `_compute_visual_tokens`, whose unsliced branch uses `allow_upscale=True` (minicpm_ocr.py:136-141). The placeholder and embedding counts disagree, which the 4.6 code itself notes makes the engine abort (minicpmv4_6.py:232-234). Images are not affected because they are counted from `tgt_sizes`. Base has no OCR model, so this is new.

**Verification:** Triggering condition: the loaded `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor` instance has a non-default `disable_small_image_upsize` or `adaptive_small_image_upsize` value, and a video has small frames that are not sliced. `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` removes the flat per-request keys and nothing else. The 4.6 `process_videos` (minicpmv4_6.py:402-407) then runs the shared image processor on each frame.

</details>

+
+class MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor(MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor):
+    def _promote_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Resolve the OCR-only upsize options into the flat form.
+
+        ``process_images`` forwards flat keys only (``_flat_processor_kwargs``
+        drops the nested scopes), and 4.6 recovers just ``downsample_mode`` /
+        ``max_slice_nums`` from the merge. Resolve the OCR options the same way
+        so that a server-level ``mm_processor_kwargs`` value, and the nested
+        ``images_kwargs`` form, both reach the image processor instead of being
+        silently dropped.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+        merged = info._merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(mm_kwargs)
+
+        promoted = {}
+        for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS:
+            value = _scoped_mm_kwarg(merged, "image", key)
+            if value is not None:
+                promoted[key] = value
+
+        if not promoted:
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {**mm_kwargs, **promoted}
+
+    def _drop_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Remove the image-only upsize options from the video path.
+
+        ``process_videos`` runs the *image* processor per frame, so a flat
+        upsize option would reach frames as well. In transformers frames go
+        through ``MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor``, which never applies these, and
+        the video placeholder is counted without them.
+        """
+        if not any(key in mm_kwargs for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS):
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {
+            key: value
+            for key, value in mm_kwargs.items()
+            if key not in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS
+        }
+
+    def process_images(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_images(
+            mm_data,
+            self._promote_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )
+
+    def process_videos(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_videos(
+            mm_data,
+            self._drop_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )
